sections.h2: Where do I take a Burke County property tax question?
sections.html:
The Burke County Tax Office works out of the Burke Services Building, 110 North Green Street, Morganton, NC 28655, from 8 am until 5 pm each weekday. The phone is (828) 764-9430, letters go to PO Box 219, Morganton, NC 28680, and Collections takes email at collections@burkenc.org.

Three divisions split the work. Real Property appraises land and buildings and fields questions on values, revaluation and appeals. Personal and Business Property takes listings and forms for taxable equipment and business assets. Collections issues bills and accepts payment for the county plus the towns and fire districts the Burke office serves, which means one bill can carry several levies.

The office also publishes its deed certification form and a tax website at burkenctax.com. A seller should start with Collections, the division that certifies the amount owed on a parcel before a deed moves on to recording.

sections.h2: What rate does Burke County levy?
sections.html:
Burke's own levy is 55.5 cents per $100 of assessed value, and the budget for fiscal 2026-2027 kept it there. That budget, about $120.7 million, passed 5-0 and began July 1, 2026.

The county says its commissioners have cut the rate twice since 2023. Your bill may list more than the county line, because town and fire district charges go through the same office. Look at each rate line for the units covering your address.

A rate multiplies a value, and the values will shift once the 2027 revaluation project is done.

Burke County is carrying out a revaluation project for 2027. Commissioners called a public hearing for November 16, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. at the Burke Services Building, to hear comment on a proposed Schedule of Values and Present Use Schedule of Values. Copies were posted online and at the tax office.

State law (G.S. 105-286) sets an eight-year ceiling between reappraisals, each as of January 1. Larger counties, those with 75,000 residents or more, can be forced to reappraise early if their sales assessment ratio drops below .85 or climbs above 1.15. The review board gets until December 1 in a revaluation year, a longer runway than usual.

For questions about the schedules, call the Tax Department at (828) 764-9430. When your new notice comes, set it beside recent sales of comparable homes nearby before deciding whether to appeal.

sections.h2: Which dates shape a Burke County tax year?
sections.html:
Bills fall due on September 1, with face-amount payment allowed until January 6. This table collects the statutory dates an owner meets.

Calendar rules that govern each Burke County tax year
EventWhat the statute saysSource
Listing windowStarts on the first business day of January and ends January 31G.S. 105-307
Bill duePayable September 1 of the fiscal yearG.S. 105-360
Par paymentPayment received ahead of January 6G.S. 105-360
First interest step2% on balances from January 6 to February 1G.S. 105-360
Ongoing interest3/4 of 1% for every month or part, after February 1G.S. 105-360
Review board opensOpens no sooner than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in MayG.S. 105-322
State-level appealNotice due within 30 days of the board's mailed decisionG.S. 105-290

Each summer the county mails listing forms for owners to update, sign and send back. Returning them within the January window avoids a late listing penalty.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Burke County value?
sections.html:
Talk to the Tax Office first. Anything unresolved goes to the review board, which is the commissioners unless the county has formed a special panel. Your request must be in hand before the panel adjourns.

  • A written request or a personal appearance both count.
  • If the board's own notice was mailed less than 15 days before adjourning, the clock gives you 15 days from that mailing.
  • The ruling arrives by mail within 30 days after adjournment.
  • Past that sits the Property Tax Commission, which takes a written notice listing your grounds, with a copy to the assessor.

Hurricane Helene created a special case. The county offered reduced values for the 2025 listing date to owners who reported unrepaired structural damage, and gave them 30 days from receipt to appeal in writing. That relief lasted a single year, so ask the Tax Office where your parcel stands now.

sections.h2: What certification does Burke County require before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Burke uses a Delinquent Tax Certification form built on G.S. 161-31, which lets commissioners instruct the register of deeds to turn away a transfer deed until the collector certifies there are no delinquent taxes. The form was revised April 22, 2026.

You supply the parcel number, the seller and buyer names, the buyer's mailing address, the site address, the price and the acreage. The form also asks if a mobile home or personal property, such as vehicles, boats or farm equipment, goes with the sale, and whether land in Present Use Value will stay enrolled. Staff then complete a ten-year grid of deferred and due taxes.

Send it to the Office of the Tax Administrator, PO Box 219, Morganton, or to collections@burkenc.org. A closing attorney often files it, though asking Collections for a figure before you list can save days.

sections.h2: Can Burke County owners get a property tax break?
sections.html:
Yes. The state's three programs apply here, filed on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, and applications must be accepted through June 1. An owner may draw on one program only.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes whichever is greater, $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent residence, for an owner at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled whose prior-year income stays within the 2026 cap of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4% of income, or 5% where income runs up to $58,200, once the owner has lived in the home five years.

Circuit breaker savings are deferred, and the tax deferred over the three prior years falls due on a transfer, an owner's death or a move out. Mention any such deferral to your closing attorney.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Burke County housing?
sections.html:
Growth is slow. The mid-2025 estimate is 88,655 people, up just 1.2% from the 2020 base and below the 90,912 counted in 2010. The county has 41,669 housing units on 506.24 land square miles.

From 2020 through 2024, 74.5% of homes were owner-occupied, valued at a median $185,400. Household income hit a median $58,592, gross rent $884, and 14.0% of people were in poverty. Adults 65 and over make up 23.2% of residents. Building permits in 2025 numbered 588. Owners with a mortgage carry a median $1,220 in monthly costs, while owners without one report $389. Workers spend a mean 23.4 minutes getting to work, and 21.0% of adults 25 and older have a bachelor's degree or higher. The county's land area is 506.24 square miles at 173.0 people per square mile.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Burke County.

faqs.q: What is Burke County's rate per $100?
faqs.a: It is 55.5 cents, unchanged for 2026-2027, plus any town or fire district charges that reach your parcel.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Burke County bill?
faqs.a: Go to 110 North Green Street in Morganton during weekday office hours, call (828) 764-9430, or email collections@burkenc.org.

faqs.q: When does interest start on Burke County bills?
faqs.a: Interest starts January 6, since payment before that date is at face amount. It is 2% through February 1 and 3/4 of 1% a month after.
Yes, a 2027 revaluation is under way. A public hearing on the proposed values was set for November 16, 2026, and state law demands reappraisal at least every eighth year.

faqs.q: Do I need tax certification to sell in Burke County?
faqs.a: Yes, the county's Delinquent Tax Certification lets the collector confirm nothing delinquent remains before the deed goes on record. Request it at collections@burkenc.org or (828) 764-9430.
